help.title: What does this do?
help.roomName: The room's name, stored on the Cube and shown by every program that talks to it.
help.comfort: The comfort temperature (sun symbol), 21.0 °C from the factory. The thermostats switch to it with their comfort/eco button.
help.eco: The eco or set-back temperature (moon symbol), for nights and absences, 17.0 °C from the factory. The thermostats switch to it with their comfort/eco button.
help.windowTemp: The temperature the radiator thermostats set while a window is open, 12 °C from the factory. A window contact in the room reports the opening as it happens; without one, a radiator thermostat detects it from a sharp fall in temperature.
help.windowMinutes: How long a radiator thermostat keeps the open-window temperature after it detected an open window itself from a sharp fall in temperature, 15 minutes from the factory; 0 switches this detection off. With a window contact in the room the thermostats ignore temperature falls and keep the open-window temperature until the window is closed.
help.maxTemp: The highest temperature that can be set on the thermostats of the room.
help.minTemp: The lowest temperature that can be set on the thermostats of the room.
help.boostMinutes: How long Boost, started with the Boost button on a thermostat, keeps the valve open: 0 to 30 minutes in steps of 5, or 60; 5 minutes from the factory. Afterwards the thermostat returns to its previous mode and temperature.
help.boostValve: How far the valve opens during Boost, 80 % from the factory.
help.decalc: Once a week the radiator thermostats open and close their valves once so that they do not calcify (descaling run); meanwhile they show “CAL” and cannot be operated. The day and hour of that run, Saturday at 12:00 from the factory.
help.maxValve: The furthest the radiator thermostats open the valve, 100 % from the factory; lower it if a radiator heats too strongly when fully open.
help.valveOffset: A percentage the radiator thermostats add to every valve position they compute while regulating. 0 % from the factory; change it only for a valve that needs it.
help.deviceName: The device's name, stored on the Cube.
help.tempOffset: Corrects the temperature this thermostat measures, from −3.5 to +3.5 °C, since the temperature next to the radiator can differ from the rest of the room. Example: set to 20 °C, but the room only reaches 18 °C: an offset of −2.0 °C. In a room with a wall thermostat the temperature is measured at the wall thermostat.
help.displayActual: The wall thermostat's display shows the measured room temperature instead of the set temperature.
help.deviceRoom: Moves the device to another room; it is then linked with the thermostats of that room and follows its settings.
help.onlyDay: On: changes apply to the edited day only. Off: changes apply to every selected day at once, the days that have the same programme.
help.poll: How often the page asks the server for the Cube's state. Changes reported by the devices arrive in between as they happen.
help.expert: Shows radio addresses, device types, the Cube's radio budget and the server version.
help.clock: The Cube keeps its own time zone. Show its clock converted to the browser's time zone, or as the Cube has it.
help.language: The language of this page. From the browser follows the browser's preferred languages; a text without a translation is shown in English.

help.cubes: The Cubes this server serves, kept in its store. A change applies at once: a new address reconnects, a new proxy address restarts that proxy, and hidden devices leave the tiles, the API and the original software. The settings file's lines only add a Cube the server does not know yet; where one differs from what is set here, the Cube says so and offers the file's value.

help.users: Everyone who signs in has one role, which says what they may do. A guest has an end date; a user without a password signs in with keys only. A password set here ends the user's sessions.
help.roles: A role is a set of capabilities, each guarding part of what the page and the API do. The six default roles can be renamed and reshaped, except the owner; more can be created. A disabled role keeps its users out.
help.capabilities: A capability switched off here is denied to every role but the owner, whatever the roles say: for example pairing while nobody should pair, or updates on a box updated by hand.
help.pairCopy: Gives the device the settings of the room's first other thermostat, as the original software does: the temperatures go to every thermostat of the room, the valve settings and the week programme to the device. It costs radio budget: about a tenth of an hour's for the temperatures and the valve settings, and 8 % for each day of the programme that differs, so up to two thirds for a new thermostat. Switched off, the device keeps its own settings.
backup.title: Backup and restore
help.backup: A backup holds the Cube's rooms, names, device settings and week programmes. Download backup saves the Cube as it is now. The server keeps backups too: after a change, by hand and before every restore. Restore… shows what it would send before anything is sent.

restore.nothing: The Cube already holds this backup: nothing to send.
